summary: Launch-Signal automation: scaffold ephemeral experiment pods (Slack channel + Confluence space + Jira sandbox) with RBAC and audit export
description:
Issue summary:
We need a new automated 'launch-signal' flow that scaffolds a short-lived experiment pod when a Product/Research lead requests a new experiment. The flow should create a Slack channel, a Confluence space + templated pages, and a Jira sandbox project with pre-seeded issue templates. The automation must enforce RBAC groups, timebound retention, and produce an audit export for compliance.

Impact:
Currently pod creation is manual and inconsistent: delays onboarding by days, misconfigured permissions leak sensitive data, and cleanup is ad-hoc. This automation will reduce lead time for experiments, enforce guardrails, and provide an auditable lifecycle.

Requirements (must-have):
- Trigger: a single form submission in Confluence/Shortcut (we prefer Confluence Create page or a small Jira intake ticket).
- Slack: create #pod-<shortname>-<team> channel, default topic, purpose, and pinned onboarding message. Channel should be private when requested. Add members from an input list and map team roles to Slack user groups.
- Confluence: create space with key POD<YYMM><id>, generate three pages from templates (Overview, Runbook, Data Access Matrix), and set space permissions: view/edit restricted to specified groups.
- Jira: create project with key POD-<shortid>, create issue templates (Experiment Plan, Data Access Request, Safety Review), and set project role mappings.
- RBAC: map requestor -> space admin, map product/eng reviewers -> space editors, create or assign ephemeral groups (ttl-bound) rather than adding individual org-wide groups.
- Timebound retention: default lifecycle 90 days; automation must include optional TTL extension workflow and automatic archival (unpublish + archive space, archive Jira project, set Slack channel to read-only and then archive).
- Audit export: create a JSON summary of actions (who triggered, resource ids, timestamps, members added/removed) and store in a central S3 bucket and Confluence audit page.
- Approvals: if data classification >= Sensitive or experiment includes private model data, require Approver group (Data Privacy / Security) to approve before provisioning.
- Notifications: notify #platform-ops and the requestor at each lifecycle stage.

Nice-to-have:
- Terraform-style declarative manifest saved in a repo (PR created automatically) representing the pod resources.
- Single-click 'teardown early' from Confluence page which triggers archive.
- Metrics emitted to observability for onboarding times and retention compliance.

Acceptance criteria:
- A PoC automation exists for a subset of teams (example: Research-UX).
- Provisioned Slack, Confluence, and Jira resources follow naming conventions and permission templates.
- TTL process runs and archives resources automatically after 90 days in a staging run.
- Audit export generated and verifiable in S3 and attached to the Confluence runbook page.
- Approval gating triggers for sensitive-data requests and blocks provisioning until approved.

Implementation notes / constraints:
- Use existing org Slack app bot; avoid creating new bot tokens. Leverage SCIM/group sync where possible.
- Confluence automation should use the Confluence Cloud REST API and page templates; avoid using server-side scripts.
- Jira provisioning must use our existing project-create automation to ensure project role mappings and permission scheme consistency.
- Keep default TTL conservative (90 days) but allow requestor to choose shorter.
- Ensure encryption and least-privilege when writing audit exports to S3.

Edge cases to handle:
- Requestor provides an email outside org: return validation error and require an org member or add-as-guest flow.
- Slack channel name collision: append numeric suffix and surface change in response to requestor.
- Approval timeouts: if approver doesn't respond within X days (configurable), escalate to Security on-call.
- Partial failures: if Slack succeeds but Confluence creation fails, automation must roll back Slack channel (or deprovision) and create a ticket in #platform-ops.

Testing plan:
- End-to-end test will run in a staging org where TTL is 1 day to validate archival, and approvals use test approver group.
- Unit tests for each API interaction and a chaos test to simulate partial failures.
- Security review of permission mappings before pilot.

Rollout plan:
1) Build PoC for Research-UX and run 10 pilot pods.
2) Collect feedback; fix permission edge cases.
3) Expand to growth/product teams behind feature flag.
4) Full rollout and document in Platform runbooks.

Owner / next steps:
- Requestor: Maya Chen (Research Platform)
- Suggested implementation owner: Platform Automation team (owner: Priya Nair)
- Next step: schedule 30m sync with Platform Automation and Security to align on approval gating and audit schema.
acceptance_criteria: PoC automation created for Research-UX; Slack/Confluence/Jira resources provision with naming and permission templates; TTL archival runs in staging; audit export appears in S3 and Confluence; approval gating blocks sensitive requests.
implementation_plan: 1) Design Confluence intake form and approval workflow. 2) Implement Slack channel creation using existing Slack app and group mapping. 3) Hook into Jira project-create API and ensure templates are seeded. 4) Implement TTL controller and archival jobs. 5) Produce audit export and secure S3 write. 6) Run staging tests and security review. 7) Pilot and roll out.
